bibliographic.title: Trustworthy Embodied Conversational Agents for Healthcare: A Design Exploration of Embodied Conversational Agents for the periconception period at Erasmus MC
bibliographic.authors: Maria Luce Lupetti, Emma Hagens, Willem van der Maden, Régine Steegers, Melek Rousian
bibliographic.venue: Proceedings of the 5th International Conference on Conversational User Interfaces, CUI 2023
bibliographic.citation_apa: Lupetti, M. L., Hagens, E., Van Der Maden, W., Steegers-Theunissen, R., & Rousian, M. (2023). Trustworthy Embodied Conversational Agents for Healthcare: A Design Exploration of Embodied Conversational Agents for the periconception period at Erasmus MC. In Proceedings of the 5th International Conference on Conversational User Interfaces, CUI 2023 Article 25 Association for Computing Machinery (ACM). https://doi.org/10.1145/3571884.3597128

methodology.method_family: Research through Design; Wizard of Oz study
methodology.study_design: Comparative prototype evaluation of chatbot and embodied conversational agent with referencing versus non-referencing conversation conditions in a tertiary hospital setting
methodology.sample_description: Participants tested in a tertiary hospital during periconception and pregnancy support context at Erasmus MC
methodology.technology_context: Embodied conversational agents, chatbots, conversational user interfaces; background discussion of generative AI and NLP for eHealth ECAs; Wizard of Oz prototypes rather than deployed LLM system

eligibility.decision_rationale: The paper provides empirical evidence on trustworthy conversational agents in a regulated healthcare setting and discusses generative AI in eHealth, but the central study is a Wizard of Oz design exploration focused on embodiment and conversational style rather than operational governance, audit, oversight, or LLM-specific controls.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only partial PDF text was supplied; governance-related claims beyond trustworthiness and brief generative-AI background need verification in full text.

appraisal.notes: Clear RtD and WoZ framing with defined prototypes and n=25, but provided excerpts do not detail analysis procedures, ethics approval, or limitations.

cerqual.explanation: Findings on trustworthiness of ECAs in hospital-based periconception support are coherent and moderately relevant to conversational governance themes, but the study is not LLM-operational and governance mechanisms such as monitoring, audit, or human oversight are not substantively evidenced in the supplied text.

coding.theme: Trustworthiness of conversational agents in healthcare
coding.subtheme: Impact of embodiment and conversational style on perceived trust

synthesis.main_claim: Limited patients' trust in ECAs may be beneficial for achieving trustworthy use of these agents in the healthcare context.
synthesis.contribution: Empirical design exploration comparing chatbot and ECA prototypes with alternative conversational styles for women during the periconception period and pregnancy in a tertiary hospital.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence on trustworthiness and design factors for conversational agents in regulated healthcare; not as primary evidence for LLM-specific conversational governance, guardrails, audit, or operational oversight.
